<a id="the-census-law--普查定律"></a>
# The census law

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`ceasing-needs-arising` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](ceasing-needs-arising.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Where what holds is listed at each step, ceasing to be recurring needs coming to be recurring; the converse fails.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. Where the members of which a determination holds are listed at each step, each once, and the determination is decided at each step, members ceasing to hold at arbitrarily late steps need members coming to hold at arbitrarily late steps. (`Becoming.Listed`, `Becoming.Listed.coming_of_ceasing`)
2. The proof goes through the census balance: with ceasing to be recurring, the ceasings from any step N on accumulate past the list at N, while the list at the end with what ceased between is the list at N with what came between, so something comes to be between. (`Becoming.recurring_accumulates`, `Becoming.Listed.over_stretch`, `Becoming.Listed.coming_iff_excess`)
3. A census is the listing of activity: under a census, ceasing recurring needs arising recurring; read of worlds, in a world with a census whose activity is decided, ceasing recurs only where arising recurs. (`Becoming.Web.Census`, `Becoming.Web.arising_of_ceasing`, `Becoming.World.Counted`, `Becoming.World.arising_of_ceasing`)
4. Read of standing: under a census of what stands, ceasing to stand recurring needs coming to stand recurring. Read of dependence: where the dependences of each step are listed, dissolving recurring needs forming recurring. (`Becoming.Web.StandingCensus`, `Becoming.Web.StandingCensus.coming_of_ceasing`, `Becoming.Web.DependenceCensus`, `Becoming.Web.DependenceCensus.forming_of_dissolving`)
5. Not conversely: accretion has a census, and arising recurs in it while nothing ever ceases; attrition keeps ceasing while nothing arises, so by this law it has no census. (`Becoming.World.accretion`, `Becoming.World.attrition`, `Becoming.Accretion.census`, `Becoming.World.census_one_way`)
6. Ceasing recurring needs coming to be recurring wherever some list covers what holds at arbitrarily late steps; a census is the case of covering every step, so the world and standing readings are corollaries of this law of laws-of-one-step. (`Becoming.coming_of_ceasing_covered`, `Becoming.Listed.covered`)
7. With no decision, where a list covers step N and nothing comes to be after it, ceasing does not recur. (`Becoming.Covers.ceasing_not_recurring`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- Listing: the members holding at each step are listed, each once, so finitely many hold at each step; there may be infinitely many members in all. The census and the census of what stands are this read of activity and of standing.
- Decidability: finding what comes to be in the pure core needs the determination decided; read of activity this is decided activity, read of standing it holds automatically (comparison of natural numbers is decidable). It is a logical commitment of the representation and classically always holds.
- census_one_way is a statement about two particular worlds, with no premise.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- The law is a count, not a mechanism: it says neither which member comes to be nor that coming to be and ceasing to be are causally linked.
- Recurring means occurring at arbitrarily late steps and gives no frequency.
- Coming to be recurring does not in general need ceasing to be recurring; it does where the list is bounded (bounded-census-keeps-pace). Witness: `Becoming.World.census_one_way`.
- **Counterexample:** accretion: a census, arising recurring, nothing ever ceasing, so the converse fails; attrition: ceasing recurring with nothing arising and no census, so the census is needed. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Openness.lean)

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used. · Contains no ethical predicate and evaluates neither arising nor ceasing. · Stated for discrete steps. · Uses decidability of the named determinations, a logical commitment written as a hypothesis. · Names follow the structural naming criteria and are adopted only where the statement has their exact meaning; readings are interpretations, open to revision.

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

In the law of a finite family (coming-and-ceasing-keep-pace: coming_recurs_iff, Web.unceasing_iff), coming to be recurs exactly when ceasing to be does; with infinitely many relata the two separate (Accretion, Attrition). This result shows that the separation needs infinity in one direction only: with finitely many holding at each step, recurring ceasing to be still needs recurring coming to be, but not conversely. The law holds of any determination whose holders are listed at each step; activity and standing are two readings of it, as that record reads one change of activity, dependence and standing. The author's reading (an AI argument): in an unfolding finite at each step there is no endless ceasing without arising; there can be endless arising without ceasing, provided the members are infinitely many in all. Arising and ceasing are names Ren confirmed (2026-10-09-arising-ceasing-names); this reading is not the proposal's generative and degenerative (Ren wrote ‘generative和degenerate虽然都在一个becoming model上，但是他们不overlap吧’, a tag question presuming that they do not overlap, so this reading is not what is meant; they read as widening and narrowing what can form, DELEGATED-CHOICES D2).
